newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agency concerned about exports to Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency concerned about exports to Hong Kong.

text.p: A U.S. congressional watchdog agency on Wednesday raised concerns about the protection of sensitive technologies exported to Hong Kong after control reverts to China.

A report by the General Accounting office, the investigative arm of Congress, said the U.S. government needed to monitor sensitive technologies exported to Hong Kong after the handover of the British colony to China on July 1.
The United States has no plans to change its less restrictive export policy toward Hong Kong after the handover, the GAO said.
"As a result, Hong Kong will continue to have easier access to sensitive technology that is more tightly controlled for China," the report said.

Businesses may export items such as titanium alloys, certain types of machine tools and high performance computers to Hong Kong without obtaining an export license, the report said. The GAO said it will be difficult to monitor whether Hong Kong would be able to control the re-export of those items to China after July 1.

"Given the decision to continue current U.S. policy toward Hong Kong, monitoring various indicators of Hong Kong's continued autonomy in export controls becomes critical to assessing the risk to U.S. nonproliferation interests," the report said.

Republican chairman of the House National Security Committee Floyd Spence of South Carolina said the United States should not only improve monitoring controlled items exported to Hong Kong, but also begin pre-license checks to determine the legitimacy of proposed end-users of controlled items. Post shipment verifications should also be into place, he said.

"I am not entirely convinced that China will respect Hong Kong's autonomy and seriously question whether Hong Kong will be able to prevent the diversion of U.S. export-controlled technology to the Chinese," he said in a statement.

"China has consistently demonstrated a willingness to divert U.S. technology to unauthorised uses as well as intent to continue the proliferation of dangerous weapons and technologies to the developing world," he added.
